title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions: response slimming and stop-heuristics consensus for stream parity
author: Aisha Raman
description: Context: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported subtle divergences in streamed payloads when tool calls and stop tokens interacted with role aliasing. Motivation: Align the stream framing, stop sentinel priority, and logprob damping so that downstream OpenAI-compatible clients see deterministic stop behavior and compact JSON payloads without duplicating role metadata. This PR implements a consensus policy that (1) coalesces adjacent empty role tokens emitted during stream stitching, (2) applies a stop-priority resolver that prefers explicit stop-array hits over heuristic token-level stop scoring, and (3) slims response envelopes by removing duplicated role/name fields in fragmented frames while preserving a final full-message envelope. Changes: runtime: stop_priority_resolver added with deterministic comparator for stop-array vs token-logprob; stream-coalescer: merges adjacent delta frames that only contain role/name to a single header frame; envelope-slimmer: drops redundant role/name on intermediate fragments, re-inserts on final flush; compatibility: chatv1 adapter mapping tweaked to prefer explicit stop matches when stop array present; tests: added regression tests for streaming a tool call followed immediately by a stop token; docs: updated API compatibility notes and streaming framing appendix. discussion: Carlos Mendez: Nice boundary work, can we make the resolver deterministic across quantized models? Requested change: include a tie-breaker based on token index.
Aisha Raman: Added tie-breaker using sequence index; updated unit test to cover quantized bytemap edge case.
Priya Shah: Integration test failing intermittently on CI with streaming timeouts — looks related to the coalescer backpressure window.
Aisha Raman: Reduced coalescer flush timeout from 30ms to 10ms and added a non-flaky test that asserts max 2-frame intermediate envelope for 512-token sequences.
Elliot Wu: Approving after seeing CI green and perf microbench results (2% p99 latency improvement on small models).
